invariant_argument: Graph admission establishes 1<=V<=64, E<=64 and valid endpoints. Outgoing lists contain original edge indices in input order; indegree counts every incoming edge, including parallel edges. In Kahn processing, residual indegree counts unprocessed incoming edges. A vertex becomes ready once, and each edge is removed once, so decrements cannot underflow and visited<=V. A successful pop order gives a strictly increasing rank on every edge. A nonempty residual finite graph with no ready vertex contains a cycle. Independent Floyd reachability checks this result.

Strict rank gives path length<V (Lean rank_length/rank_bound/rank_no_cycle). Enumeration starts with every vertex identity and extends every discovered prefix by each matching outgoing edge. Induction on word length proves completeness on successful exhaustion; unique prefix and final edge ID prove uniqueness of each (source,word). Parallel edges remain distinct generators. BFS order is length, then source and edge-word order. The count starts at V<=budget and is checked before every push, so count<=budget<=64 throughout. Refusal exposes no truncated category.

The mathematical graph has finite vertex IDs and typed generator IDs with fixed boundaries. Rust chronological words refine Quiver.Path.nil/cons. A source and generator word determine a unique typed path and end vertex. The Lean edgeWord function records chronological labels, proves concatenation and length, and connects to the actual Mathlib path category. This is a source/native representation argument, not extracted Rust code or an unbounded graph claim.

Borrowed lookup has the same usize/word lexicographic key equality as the original owned BTreeMap. Unique sorted keys retain original path indices. Composable concatenation is a valid DAG path, and complete enumeration guarantees lookup succeeds. Clearing one scratch vector and appending both words gives the original concatenation. Cached v/p labels have exactly the original values. Allocation order changes, but there are no user callbacks or mutable inputs whose successful result depends on that order.

Identity index v labels arrow p{v} at object v{v}; every other path has its exact outer boundary. The declared composition domain consists of exactly the compatible pairs, with result the unique concatenated word. Empty words give both units, and list append gives associativity. The actual finite-category validator independently checks the declaration before ownership is exposed. Matrix and declared cells use the same i,j,k, so the index API agrees with the held certificate. Missing closure or validation failure returns a typed error.

FinitePathCategory and FinitePath fields are private. There is no unchecked/default/Deserialize constructor or mutable accessor. The owner retains the graph, complete paths, composition matrix and actual ValidatedFiniteCategory. Shared getters and Clone preserve this context; consuming a separately cloned certificate cannot mutate the owner. Checked public queries refuse unknown indices. None composition means noncomposability. Counts and all private indices are bounded by V,E,P<=64.

Mathlib Paths and lift_unique establish the mathematical free-category universal property. The finite DAG representation above connects the delivered construction to that theorem. There is no new Rust functor-lift API. L5 describes the owned certificate architecture and theorem-matching abstraction, not a module title or size. MAX_PATHS is an execution cap; acyclicity and strict rank provide mathematical finiteness.

All phases preserve the original public constructor result and error precedence: graph/cycle admission and prefix BFS are unchanged; borrowed lookup, cached labels and scratch concatenation produce the same words, indices, names and compositions. This preservation assumes standard allocation succeeds, not that OOM is a typed PathError. Unreachable defensive error remaps were not counted as non-equivalent public-domain faults.
cost_review: V,E,P<=64 and maximum word length D<V. Graph indexing is O(V+E); Kahn processing with its ordered ready set is O((V+E)log(V+1)). Each newly stored path requires an owned prefix copy and final edge, so enumeration stores the necessary sum of path lengths. No whole graph or topological inventory is copied per path.

Borrowed lookup stores P reference/index rows and sorts in O(P log P) comparisons, each costing at most O(D). Composition considers P² pairs, reuses one O(D) scratch vector and performs O(log P) word comparisons for compatible pairs. A conservative bound is O(P² D log(P+1)), plus category-table insertion and required output bytes. The P² matrix is required stored output; path keys and concatenation vectors are not reallocated per pair.

Object/path names are formatted V+P times outside composition loops. The canonical category provider owns the required arrow data and composition keys/values; no repeated format-then-copy temporaries remain in the inner loop. Actual category admission checks names, complete domain, boundaries, units and compatible triples; a conservative O(P³ log(P+1)) query bound includes string comparisons. Its implementation is separately reviewed.

Public path/compose queries use checked O(1) vector access. edge_path scans at most P one-edge comparisons without allocating a word. Origin counts take O(V+P). Other getters borrow in O(1). Standard Clone/Debug/Eq costs the stored graph, word, table and String data. Finite caps do not guarantee allocator availability or a fixed latency.
